author: Roszczyk
title: Debian Packages job fails - apt-get cannot reach azure.archive.ubuntu.com (connection timeout)
signature: Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com connection timed out|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get install of build-essential and related packages fails with repeated connection timeouts to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80

key_errors:
Err:1 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble/main amd64 build-essential amd64 12.10ubuntu1
  Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80 (52.250.76.244), connection timed out

E: Failed to fetch http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/b/build-essential/build-essential_12.10ubuntu1_amd64.deb  Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80 (52.250.76.244), connection timed out
E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt-get update or try with --fix-missing?
root_cause: The 'Test debian packages' step in the Debian Packages job runs apt-get install inside an Ubuntu 24.04 docker container that resolves the Azure-hosted Ubuntu mirror (azure.archive.ubuntu.com). The mirror connection to 52.250.76.244:80 timed out repeatedly (over a 6+ minute fetch window) while downloading build-essential and its dependencies, causing apt to report exit code 100. This is a transient network/infrastructure issue in the GitHub-hosted runner's egress path or the Azure mirror itself, unrelated to the PR's GPU grid_sample kernel changes, which were not involved in this job's test steps.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reliably reproducible locally; depends on transient network connectivity between the GitHub Actions runner and azure.archive.ubuntu.com at the time of the run. Can be approximated by running the job_debian_packages.yml workflow's 'Test debian packages' step in a container under congested or unstable network conditions.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job; this is a known recurring transient apt-mirror connectivity issue (9th occurrence).

Consider adding retry/backoff logic (e.g., apt-get with -o Acquire::Retries=3) or a fallback mirror in the Debian Packages Dockerfile/workflow to reduce sensitivity to azure.archive.ubuntu.com outages.
If this mirror continues to be unreliable, consider pinning a different apt mirror or using a cached/local apt proxy for CI runners.
prevention_strategies: Add apt-get retry configuration (Acquire::Retries, Acquire::http::Timeout) and/or a secondary mirror fallback in the Debian Packages job's Dockerfile so transient mirror outages don't fail the whole merge-queue run. Consider monitoring azure.archive.ubuntu.com reachability from GitHub-hosted runners given its recurrence (9+ times in recent weeks).
historical_context: This exact signature (apt-get timeout connecting to azure.archive.ubuntu.com during the Debian Packages job) has now been recorded 9 times historically (pattern 7d2e2ff59d37c6b4, first seen 2026-08-18), plus several closely related but distinct signatures for the same job (DNS resolution failures, connection refused, InRelease fetch failures) totaling 10+ Network-category pattern records tied to apt mirror connectivity in this CI pipeline. This recurrence suggests the underlying Azure Ubuntu mirror or runner network path is a persistent source of flakiness for this specific job.
